enquiry: Our research group is evaluating a spectral measurement interface using model biological tissues such as chicken muscle, fat and liver. We want to compare MIR ATR and fluorescence information, because the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location. This is a laboratory classification study. We need a first comparison experiment and a clear statement of what its results would demonstrate.

clarification_questions.question: What classification decision should the comparison support, and what would be done differently if the classes were reliably separated?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the purpose of the classification and what the experiment must demonstrate.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Purpose unclear; the first experiment is a feasibility screen of whether MIR ATR and fluorescence separate the tissue types in the lab.

clarification_questions.question: Which tissue classes must be distinguished (for example muscle, fat, liver, or other) and how are they defined for the reference labels?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the classification task and the labels against which both methods are judged.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Classes not defined; the first experiment uses the three named tissues as provisional classes.

clarification_questions.question: Which fluorescent species do you expect in these tissues or in the model samples, and is any fluorescent indicator added?
clarification_questions.why: Fluorescence only measures a defined fluorescent species or a justified indicator; this decides whether fluorescence is a meaningful input.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Fluorescent species unknown; lab screening first establishes whether the fluorescence signal carries class information.

clarification_questions.question: How are the tissue samples prepared (fresh, frozen, minced, cut into blocks) and how long do they stay stable before measurement?
clarification_questions.why: Sample form and age affect ATR contact, fluorescence and spectral stability, and therefore the comparison.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Preparation and stability unknown; the protocol is fixed and documented before any measurement.

clarification_questions.question: How heterogeneous is the material within a sample (fat and muscle layers, marbling, surface texture), and what sampling spot size is needed?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether same-spot measurement is needed and how many measurement locations are required.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Heterogeneity level unknown; same-spot measurement is tested as a condition of the design.

clarification_questions.question: What is the existing or planned measurement interface (ATR probe, combi probe, bench accessory) and do you have MIR-compatible fibers or a bench FTIR?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether MIR ATR and fluorescence can measure the same spot and what fibers are needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Interface and fibers unknown; the design assumes a bench setup with same-spot measurement, with fiber needs checked later.

clarification_questions.question: What reference method, such as histology or a chemical assay, provides the class labels for each sample, and how accurate is it?
clarification_questions.why: Without a reference, classification performance cannot be judged.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference not defined; the first experiment requires a defined reference before any model is evaluated.

clarification_questions.question: What performance is needed for the classification (accuracy, error types, number of runs) and what is the timeline?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the acceptance criteria for the comparison and the scope of the experiment.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Performance criteria unknown; the first experiment reports single-method and combined results against the reference without a threshold.

flags_before_revision.detail: overstated: The claim says fluorescence 'separated' liver. S04 p.4 says fluorescence is 'well suited for the recognition of liver tissue' and that no individual technique was sufficient to completely separate the three classes. Fix: Replace 'separated liver' with wording such as 'fluorescence was well suited for recognising liver tissue, though no single technique fully separated the three classes'.

not_supported: S04 p.3 discusses heterogeneity of fat samples and says it explains low reproducibility. It does not mention cut-surface inhomogeneity, nor say that heterogeneity can mimic class differences. Fix: Limit the risk to what the page states: tissue heterogeneity (e.g., fat) can cause low measurement reproducibility. Remove the cut-surface and class-mimicking claims or source them separately.

not_supported: S02 p.6 gives only the transmission ranges of each fiber type. It does not classify fibers as 'full range' or 'partial' for MIR or fluorescence, nor state that no single fiber covers the MIR range. Fix: Present the transmission ranges from the chart directly and label the full/partial coverage as an inference from those ranges, not as a rule stated on the page.

rule_hints: fluorescence_needs_fluorophore: Fluorescence only measures a defined fluorescent species or a justified indicator; most chemicals do not fluoresce. [S01 p.5; S04 p.4; DOCX §5]
sensitivity_not_selectivity: High sensitivity does not imply selectivity. Fluorimetry and UV/Vis are rated high sensitivity but low selectivity. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); DOCX §5]
nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]
combination_is_hypothesis: Combining methods can add complementary information, but the gain is a hypothesis to test against the best single method. [S01 p.7-8; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [DOCX §3]
